name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,830

entries.clue: Papal candidate elected on paper by majority of total (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry what is placed on something sits after it, so the paper leads and the winner follows
indicatorNotes.majority of: a majority is more than half but short of the whole, so the word beside it arrives with its ending gone

blocks.note: card is stiff paper, the stuff a postcard is cut from
the candidate who wins is in, as in 'the Tories are in'
total is ALL, and most of it is its first two letters

annotation.surface: A candidate for the papacy elected on paper by most of the votes cast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across entry puts the piece named first second in the grid, so the paper goes in ahead of it. The men who elect a pope are also the men he is chosen from.
annotation.definitionFit: A pope is chosen from the College of Cardinals, so every cardinal is a standing candidate for the job.

entries.clue: Sun god's head surrounded by halo every so often (6)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: to be surrounded is to have something on either side, so the piece named first is closed in by the letters that follow
indicatorNotes.every so often: every so often is now and then rather than all the way through, so only every second letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: taking hALO every other letter from the second gives A and O
a poll is a head, the sense that survives in poll tax and in counting heads at a polling station

annotation.surface: A god of the sun shown with his head ringed by a halo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not an instruction to take a first letter, which is the trap: it is a whole word meaning the thing on your shoulders. The halo hands over only its second and fourth letters, and they part to let the head in.
annotation.definitionFit: Apollo drove the sun across the sky in Greek myth, so the definition is by example: one sun god standing for the class.

entries.clue: Dave's outside bar before woman who's not appeared yet (9)

indicatorNotes.outside: the outside of a name is the pair of letters at its ends, and only those two are wanted

blocks.note: the ends of DAVE are D and E
bar means except, as in 'all bar one', and so does but
ante is Latin for before, the ante- of antenatal

annotation.surface: Dave stands outside the bar waiting for a woman who still has not turned up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is the conjunction meaning except, not the place the surface has Dave standing outside. Ante keeps its Latin sense in English only in compounds, which is why it is easy to miss on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman on the brink of her formal presentation to society, so the appearance she is named for is still to come.

entries.clue: Getting hitched, said Hugh finally - bad follow-up to Four Weddings? (7,4)

indicatorNotes.said: what is said is heard rather than spelt, so this piece is wanted as a sound and not as its own letters
indicatorNotes.finally: finally is at the very end, so only the last letter of the name beside it is taken

blocks.note: tying the knot is getting hitched, and the K of knotting is silent
the closing letter of HUGH
ill means bad, as in ill health and ill luck

annotation.surface: Hugh announcing at last that he is getting married, dismissed as a poor sequel to Four Weddings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad' reads as the verdict on the sequel and is three of its letters. Hugh Grant starred in both films, so the name doing the announcing on the surface is the one that ties the two pictures together.
annotation.definitionFit: Notting Hill, the Richard Curtis film of 1999, was the picture that followed Four Weddings and a Funeral, and it takes its name from the district of west London.

entries.clue: Lecture successful business student enters at the end (7)

indicatorNotes.enters: to enter a place is to go inside it, so these letters are set within the word named after them

blocks.note: whatever comes at the end is the last of them
the business student who passes comes out with an MBA, a Master of Business Administration

annotation.surface: A business student who has done well slipping into the lecture just as it finishes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' is the verb meaning to scold, not the hour in a hall the surface has the student sneaking into. Three letters of a postgraduate degree do all the work in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: To lambast someone is to lay into them at length, which is what lecturing them means when the sense is a dressing-down.

entries.clue: Fill out promissory note without reflecting (6)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: a reflection shows a thing the other way round, so those letters are read back to front

blocks.note: a bill is a written undertaking to pay
w/o is the everyday shorthand for without

annotation.surface: Filling in an IOU without stopping to think about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without reflecting' reads as acting on impulse and is two instructions: the shorthand first, then a turn. Each word of the clue after the definition does a separate job, which is what makes it read as a single phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A sail or a curtain billows when it swells in the wind, which is what it is to fill out.

entries.clue: Scratching both sides, curse wide vehicle (3)

indicatorNotes.Scratching: to scratch an entry is to strike it off, so the letters named beside it are struck off the word

blocks.note: to abuse someone is to curse at them
the two sides of ABUSE are the A at the front and the E at the back

annotation.surface: Cursing a wide vehicle that has been scraped along both its sides.
annotation.walkthrough: The scratching in the picture is paintwork and in the parse it is letters, which is what keeps the surface still. Both sides of a word means its first letter and its last, never its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A bus is one of the widest things on an ordinary road, so the definition names it by the room it takes up.

entries.clue: Many love young man's trousers (5)

indicatorNotes.trousers: to trouser a fiver is to pocket it, and what is pocketed disappears inside

blocks.note: a young man is a lad, and the clue's own apostrophe-s supplies the last letter
love is nothing in tennis scoring, and nothing is written O

annotation.surface: Plenty of people admiring a young man's trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is the verb, and a verb cannot be the garment the surface is admiring. O for love comes from the tennis court, where love is a score of nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: Loads of something is a great quantity of it, as in 'loads of people turned up'.

entries.clue: Obvious question, tax too much? (8)

blocks.note: overt means out in the open, the opposite of covert
to question somebody is to ask them

annotation.surface: The obvious question at election time: are taxes too high?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' is the verb meaning to make demands on someone's strength, not the money the surface is arguing about. The question mark is the setter flagging that stretched sense as deliberate.
annotation.definitionFit: To overtask someone is to set them more than they can manage, which is taxing them too much in the sense of straining them.

entries.clue: Groom with fine teeth initially averse to fighting (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially is at the start, so only the opening letters of the words beside it are taken

blocks.note: the thing you groom with, and the one whose teeth are described as fine
the opening letters of these two words

annotation.surface: A well-groomed sort who has never had any appetite for a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is the verb here, so neither the bridegroom nor the stable hand is wanted. 'Initially' looks forwards, not back: the two letters come from the words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting of the armed kind — troops in combat are troops engaged in it.

entries.clue: White male American trainee learning how to use guns? (8)

blocks.note: m is the standing short form for male, as on any form
US stands for the United States and so for American

blocks.clueFragment: trainee learning how to use guns
blocks.note: a cadet is a trainee in the forces or the police, taught to shoot early on

annotation.surface: A white American man on a course learning to handle firearms.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one American stereotype, and every word of it turns out to be a separate piece of the parse. The wine is the dry white made around Nantes, at the mouth of the Loire.
annotation.definitionFit: Muscadet is the crisp dry white of the western Loire, so 'white' is the drinker's word for the thing itself.

entries.clue: Scheme of random selection to succeed Papa (4)

indicatorNotes.to succeed: to succeed somebody is to come after them, so these letters follow the one named beside them

blocks.note: Papa is P in the radio alphabet
choosing by lot is choosing at random

annotation.surface: A scheme to pick the next pope by drawing names out of a hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papa' is the radio alphabet's P, though this puzzle's run of popes would rather it were the man himself. Drawing lots is the oldest random selection there is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret scheme — the plot to blow up Parliament was exactly that.

entries.clue: For replacement, is antipope unsuitable? (10)

indicatorNotes.For replacement: a thing put up for replacement is not going to stay as it is, and neither do these letters stay in the order given

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Asking whether an antipope is the wrong man to put in the pope's place.
annotation.walkthrough: An antipope is a rival claimant elected against the sitting pope, so a clue about replacements is exactly where he belongs. The opening two words have to be read as an instruction to the letters rather than as a description of the man.
annotation.definitionFit: Something inapposite is out of place or beside the point, which is what unsuitable means of a remark or a choice.

entries.clue: Estate Golf outside home, fair extra cost to motorist? (7,4)

indicatorNotes.outside: what stands outside goes round the outside, so the letters named first close over the one named next

blocks.note: the grounds round a country house are its park
Golf is G in the radio alphabet
somebody at home is in
fine weather is fair weather

annotation.surface: A Golf estate standing outside the house on a fair day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Estate Golf' reads as the estate version of a Volkswagen and is two unrelated pieces, one of them a radio alphabet letter. The two that close over 'home' are split, one on each side of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A parking fine is the penalty ticket a driver picks up on top of what the parking itself costs, which no trip ever budgets for.

entries.clue: Trifle's quality resonating with us cooks (12)

indicatorNotes.cooks: a cook stirs the ingredients together, and what comes out is not in the order it went in

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters
two more letters joined to the fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: The quality of a trifle striking a chord with those of us who cook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' is the small nothing of no importance, not the pudding the cooks have brought in. Nugatory is the adjective behind the answer: a nugatory objection is one not worth making.
annotation.definitionFit: Nugatoriness is the state of amounting to a trifle — of being worth nothing at all.

entries.clue: Church going up, built right inside school (5,4)

indicatorNotes.going up: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom of the grid towards the top, so the letters arrive back to front
indicatorNotes.inside: what is inside a word sits between its letters, so these pieces are posted into the one named last

blocks.note: Eton is the boarding school by the Thames, and crosswords' first choice for school
a thing built is a thing made
r is the standing short form for right

annotation.surface: A church going up, built right in the middle of a school.
annotation.walkthrough: Two separate pieces are posted into the school one after the other, and only then is the whole string read upwards. 'Going up' can mean a turn at all because this entry runs down the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the cathedral on the Île de la Cité in Paris, so the definition is by example: one church standing for the class.

entries.clue: A VIP organised celebrity team building (8)

indicatorNotes.organised: something organised has been put into an arrangement it did not have before, and so have these letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, four letters
a social lion is a celebrity, the person everybody wants at their party

annotation.surface: A VIP and a celebrity signed up for a spot of team building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Team building' is the corporate away-day on the surface and a building for a team in the parse. Lion for a celebrity is Victorian usage that crosswords have kept alive.
annotation.definitionFit: The pavilion at a cricket ground is the building where the teams change and sit waiting to bat.

entries.clue: King in utopia recalled unforgiving mountainous country (4,8)

indicatorNotes.in: what is in a thing is set between its letters rather than beside them
indicatorNotes.recalled: to recall something is to call it back, so its letters come back the other way about

blocks.note: an ideal is a utopia, the perfect state nobody has reached
k is the standing short form for king, as on a chessboard
a strict parent is unforgiving of slips

annotation.surface: A king living in utopia casts his mind back to a harsh mountain country.
annotation.walkthrough: The king goes in after the turn, not before: utopia is reversed first and he is posted into what is left. 'Recalled' does duty twice, as the surface's act of memory and as the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lake District is the mountainous corner of north-west England, Scafell Pike and Helvellyn included, and 'country' is the walker's sense of a tract of land rather than a nation.

entries.clue: Twitcher stumbles across corncrake in the Borders (7)

indicatorNotes.across: a thing laid across another lies over it from one side to the other, so this word closes over the letters named next
indicatorNotes.in the Borders: the borders of a word are the letters at its two edges, and only those are taken

blocks.note: to trip is to stumble
the outermost letters of CORNCRAKE

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher comes upon a corncrake in the Scottish Borders.
annotation.walkthrough: A twitcher is a birdwatcher who chases rarities, and the Borders are the hill country either side of the Scotland-England line, so the surface is a real birding story. The definition wants a thing that twitches instead.
annotation.definitionFit: The triceps is a muscle, and a muscle is the thing that twitches — the birdwatcher lives on the surface only.

entries.clue: Sheep boxed by boomer in Oz (6)

indicatorNotes.boxed by: whatever is boxed by something is shut inside it whole, letters and order untouched

blocks.note: the letters run straight on across the gaps of booMER IN Oz

annotation.surface: A sheep being boxed by a big kangaroo out in Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxed' is the kangaroo's own verb, which is what makes the picture stand up, and it is also the instruction. A boomer is a full-grown male kangaroo and Oz is Australia, so the surface is entirely at home.
annotation.definitionFit: The merino is the fine-woolled breed Australia built its wool trade on, so the definition is by example.

entries.clue: Divorcing princess, gnome pockets £50 (10)

indicatorNotes.pockets: to pocket something is to take it in and keep it, so what follows goes inside

blocks.note: Di was Diana, Princess of Wales, and she is crosswords' standing princess
a gnome is a pithy saying, from the Greek for a maxim — the sense behind gnomic
£ is L for pound and 50 is L in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Divorcing a princess, a garden gnome pockets fifty pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The gnome is not the one on the lawn but the old word for a maxim. The money is two Ls doing different jobs: the pound sign and the Roman fifty.
annotation.definitionFit: To disally is to break off an alliance, and the alliance a divorce breaks is a marriage.

entries.clue: Rep theatre in London, years earlier (5)

indicatorNotes.earlier: in a down entry what comes earlier sits higher, so these letters are written in first

blocks.note: an age is a long span of years
the NT is the National Theatre on the South Bank

annotation.surface: A repertory company at a London theatre in years gone by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rep theatre' reads as repertory and is really two clues end to end: the rep is the definition, the theatre is the London one. The NT is the concrete block on the South Bank that everybody argues about.
annotation.definitionFit: A rep is the representative who acts on your behalf, which is the job an agent does for a writer or an actor.

entries.clue: First Lady Republican at all times (4)

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in the Genesis story
R is the standing short form for a Republican, as on a US ballot

annotation.surface: The First Lady has always been a Republican.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' is the White House title on the surface and the first woman of all in the parse. Genesis, not Washington, is where she comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times — the ever-present risk is the one present at every moment.

entries.clue: Terrier was shown something brown to drink (8)

blocks.note: a programme that was shown was aired
brown ale is the dark bottled beer of the north of England

annotation.surface: A terrier being offered something brown to drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was shown' is broadcasting, not the dog show the surface would like to put the terrier into. Brown ale is dark, sweetish bottled beer, a northern English institution.
annotation.definitionFit: The Airedale is the largest of the terrier breeds, named after the Yorkshire dale of the river Aire, so the definition is by example.

entries.clue: Dust to clean with wife away (3)

indicatorNotes.away: someone away is not there, so the letter named beside it is missing from the word

blocks.note: to wash a thing is to clean it
w is the standing short form for wife

annotation.surface: Dusting the house while the wife is away.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface leaves a man at home with the chores, and it is the chore that loses a letter rather than the person. W for wife keeps company with H for husband in the same short list.
annotation.definitionFit: Ash is the fine grey dust a fire leaves behind — ashes to ashes, dust to dust.

entries.clue: Henry is forgotten by people before long (2,1,3)

indicatorNotes.is forgotten by: what is forgotten has gone missing, so the letter named goes missing from the word that follows

blocks.note: to people a place is to inhabit it
the henry is the unit of inductance, written H

annotation.surface: A king called Henry whom everybody has forgotten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'People' is the verb, to populate, and as a noun it leads nowhere at all — that is the whole disguise. The henry is the SI unit of inductance, named after Joseph Henry.
annotation.definitionFit: In a bit means shortly: 'see you in a bit' is see you before long.

entries.clue: Canary egg brought into school (6)

indicatorNotes.brought into: what is brought into a place ends up inside it, so these letters go between the ones named next

blocks.note: sch is the standing short form for school
a nit is the egg a head louse lays

annotation.surface: A child carrying a canary's egg into school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canary' is the informer, from singing like one, not the bird whose egg the child is carrying. A nit is a louse's egg, which is exactly what a school is famous for.
annotation.definitionFit: A canary is somebody who sings to the police, and a snitch is the informer who does the singing.

entries.clue: Steel OK to fashion new frame (8)

indicatorNotes.to fashion: to fashion something is to work it into a shape it did not have, which is what happens to these letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, seven letters
n is the standing short form for new
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Signing off the steel for a new frame to be made up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New' is not describing the frame; it is the eighth letter of the fodder, and it hides because steel and frames belong together. The OK is fodder too, which is why the clue can afford to look like a note from a site foreman.
annotation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the frame a body is built on, and the same word does for the steel frame of a building.
